Deployment.description: Manages a set of identical Pods, ensuring a desired number are always running. Supports rolling updates, rollbacks, and scaling. Ideal for stateless applications where any Pod can handle any request.

keyFields.description: Number of identical Pod copies to keep running at all times.
Label query used to identify which Pods belong to this Deployment. Must match the Pod template labels.
Blueprint for each Pod: defines containers, images, ports, env vars, volumes, and probes.
How Pods are replaced during updates. RollingUpdate (default) replaces Pods gradually with zero downtime; Recreate kills all old Pods before starting new ones.
CPU/memory requests (guaranteed) and limits (maximum) for each container. Required for autoscaling and scheduling.
Kubelet uses this probe to decide when to restart a container. Fails → container restarts.
Kubelet uses this probe to decide when a container is ready to receive traffic. Fails → removed from Service endpoints.

StatefulSet.description: Like a Deployment but for stateful applications. Each Pod gets a stable, unique identity (name + DNS) and persistent storage that survives restarts. Pods are created and deleted in order.
useCases: Any app that needs stable network identity

keyFields.description: Name of the Headless Service that governs this StatefulSet. Required — provides stable DNS for each Pod (pod-0.svc, pod-1.svc, …).
Number of Pods. Created in order (0, 1, 2…) and deleted in reverse order.
Must match the Pod template labels.
PVC template automatically provisioned per Pod. Each Pod gets its own persistent volume that survives Pod rescheduling.
RollingUpdate (default) updates Pods one at a time in reverse order. OnDelete requires manual Pod deletion to trigger updates.

DaemonSet.description: Ensures exactly one Pod runs on every (or selected) Node in the cluster. When new Nodes join, a Pod is automatically scheduled on them. When Nodes are removed, the Pod is garbage collected.

keyFields.description: Identifies which Pods are managed by this DaemonSet.
Pod template. No replicas field — the scheduler ensures one Pod per node.
RollingUpdate replaces Pods one node at a time. OnDelete requires manual Pod deletion.
Optional: restrict to specific nodes by label (e.g., only GPU nodes or specific OS).
Allow the DaemonSet Pod to be scheduled on tainted nodes (e.g., master nodes with NoSchedule taint).

ReplicaSet.description: Maintains a stable number of identical Pod replicas at any given time. Usually managed by a Deployment — create a ReplicaSet directly only when you need low-level control without the Deployment update machinery.
useCases: Pinned Pod version with no update lifecycle

keyFields.description: Desired number of Pods. The ReplicaSet controller reconciles this continuously.
Selects which Pods this ReplicaSet owns. Pods matching this selector but not owned are adopted.
Pod template. Unlike Deployment, changes here do NOT trigger rolling updates — existing Pods are not replaced.

Job.description: Runs one or more Pods to completion. Unlike Deployments, Jobs are not restarted after they succeed — they terminate when the desired number of completions is reached.

keyFields.description: Total number of successful Pod completions required. Default: 1.
Number of Pods that may run simultaneously. Useful for parallel batch work.
Number of retries before the Job is considered failed. Default: 6.
Job-level timeout: terminates the Job after this many seconds regardless of retries.
Must be Never or OnFailure. OnFailure restarts the same Pod; Never creates a new Pod on failure.

CronJob.description: Runs Jobs on a repeating schedule using standard Unix cron syntax. Creates a new Job object at each scheduled time. Use for periodic tasks that should run automatically.

keyFields.description: Cron expression defining when Jobs are created. Format: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. Example: '0 2 * * *' = 2am daily.
Job template created on each schedule trigger. Same spec as a regular Job.
Allow (default): concurrent Jobs permitted. Forbid: skip new Job if previous still running. Replace: cancel previous Job and start new one.
Number of successful Job records to retain. Default: 3.
Number of failed Job records to retain. Default: 1.
How many seconds past a scheduled time the Job can still start before being skipped.

Service.description: Provides a stable network endpoint (IP + DNS) to reach a dynamic set of Pods. Since Pods are ephemeral and their IPs change, Services act as a reliable load-balanced entry point.

keyFields.description: ClusterIP (default): internal cluster IP only. NodePort: exposes on each Node's IP at a static port. LoadBalancer: provisions a cloud load balancer. ExternalName: maps to a DNS name.
Label query to identify target Pods. Traffic is load-balanced across all matching Pods that pass readiness checks.
Port the Service listens on (what clients connect to).
Port on the Pod that traffic is forwarded to. Defaults to the same as port.
NodePort type only: static port (30000–32767) exposed on every Node's external IP.
Headless Service — no virtual IP, returns Pod IPs directly. Used with StatefulSets for stable DNS per Pod.

Ingress.description: Manages external HTTP/HTTPS access to Services inside the cluster. Acts as a reverse proxy router — maps hostnames and URL paths to backend Services. Requires an Ingress Controller (nginx, traefik, etc.) to be installed.
useCases: Single entry point for multiple services
Replacing multiple LoadBalancer Services with one

keyFields.description: Which Ingress Controller handles this resource (e.g. nginx, traefik, alb). Replaces the deprecated annotation.
Hostname to match (e.g. api.example.com). Omit for a wildcard rule.
URL path prefix or exact path to match.
Prefix: /foo matches /foo, /foo/bar. Exact: /foo matches only /foo. ImplementationSpecific: controller decides.
Enables HTTPS. References a Secret containing the TLS certificate and private key. Causes HTTP → HTTPS redirect.
Controller-specific settings (rate limiting, auth, rewrites, etc.) injected as annotations. Syntax varies by controller.

ConfigMap.description: Stores non-sensitive configuration data as key-value pairs. Decouples configuration from container images so you can change config without rebuilding. Pods consume ConfigMaps as environment variables, command-line args, or mounted files.

keyFields.description: String key-value pairs. Values can be simple strings or multi-line files (use | for block literals).
Base64-encoded binary values (images, certificates). Keys must be different from data keys.
Set to true to prevent any changes after creation. Improves performance by removing watches — use for static config.
Inject all keys as environment variables into a container.
Mount keys as files in a directory inside the container. Changes to the ConfigMap are reflected within ~60s.

Secret.description: Stores sensitive data (passwords, tokens, keys) separately from Pod specs. Data is base64-encoded (not encrypted by default — use Sealed Secrets or KMS for encryption at rest). Pods reference Secrets without embedding credentials in manifests.

keyFields.description: Opaque (default): arbitrary data. kubernetes.io/tls: TLS cert + key. kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson: registry auth. kubernetes.io/service-account-token: SA tokens.
Base64-encoded key-value pairs. Encode values with: echo -n 'value' | base64
Plain-text key-value pairs (not base64). Kubernetes encodes them on write. Convenient for creating Secrets without manual encoding.
Prevents modifications after creation. Improves cluster performance for Secrets that should never change.

StorageClass.description: Defines a class of storage with specific provisioner and parameters. When a PVC references a StorageClass, the provisioner dynamically creates a PersistentVolume matching the PVC's request. Eliminates the need to pre-provision storage manually.
useCases: Defining fast vs. slow storage tiers
Cloud provider disk types (gp3, io1, premium)

keyFields.description: CSI driver or in-tree provisioner that creates the volume. Examples: ebs.csi.aws.com, disk.csi.azure.com, pd.csi.storage.gke.io, kubernetes.io/no-provisioner (manual).
Provisioner-specific settings passed to the driver. Examples: type=gp3, fsType=ext4, replication-type=regional-pd.
What happens to the PV when its PVC is deleted. Delete (default): PV and backing storage are removed. Retain: PV and data are kept (manual cleanup required).
Immediate (default): PV provisioned as soon as PVC is created. WaitForFirstConsumer: PV provisioned only when a Pod using the PVC is scheduled — ensures volume is in the same zone as the Pod.
Set to true to allow users to resize PVCs backed by this StorageClass. The CSI driver must also support expansion.
Options passed to the mount command when attaching the volume (e.g. hard, nfsvers=4.1). Unsupported options cause mount to fail.

PersistentVolumeClaim.description: A request for storage by a user. Like a Pod consuming node resources, a PVC consumes PV resources. Kubernetes binds the PVC to a suitable PersistentVolume (static) or triggers dynamic provisioning via a StorageClass.

keyFields.description: ReadWriteOnce (RWO): mounted read-write by a single node — most block storage. ReadOnlyMany (ROX): mounted read-only by many nodes. ReadWriteMany (RWX): mounted read-write by many nodes — requires NFS/CephFS. ReadWriteOncePod (RWOP): single Pod only (K8s 1.22+).
Amount of storage requested (e.g. 5Gi, 100Mi). The bound PV must be at least this size.
Which StorageClass to use for dynamic provisioning. Leave empty to use the cluster default. Set to '' to disable dynamic provisioning (bind to existing PV only).
Filesystem (default): volume is formatted and mounted as a directory. Block: volume is exposed as a raw block device to the Pod.
Bind only to PVs matching these labels. Useful for static binding to a specific pre-provisioned PV.
Directly bind to a specific PV by name, bypassing selector matching.

VolumeSnapshot.description: Requests a point-in-time snapshot of a PersistentVolumeClaim. The snapshot can be used to create new PVCs (restore data), clone volumes, or back up data. Requires a CSI driver that supports snapshots.

keyFields.description: Which VolumeSnapshotClass (and CSI driver) handles this snapshot. Determines snapshot storage backend and deletion policy.
PVC to snapshot. Used when dynamically creating a new snapshot from an existing volume.
Pre-existing VolumeSnapshotContent to bind to. Used for importing snapshots that already exist in the storage backend.
Becomes true when the snapshot is fully taken and available to restore from.
To restore: create a PVC with spec.dataSource.name pointing to this VolumeSnapshot — Kubernetes provisions a new volume pre-populated with snapshot data.

VolumeSnapshotContent.description: Cluster-scoped resource representing an actual snapshot in the storage backend. Like a PersistentVolume for snapshots — VolumeSnapshots bind to VolumeSnapshotContents. Created automatically when you take a snapshot, or manually for pre-provisioned snapshots.

keyFields.description: Delete: removes the snapshot from storage when the VolumeSnapshotContent is deleted. Retain: keeps the storage snapshot even after the object is deleted.
CSI driver name that manages this snapshot (must match VolumeSnapshotClass driver).
Pre-provisioned: the ID/handle of an existing snapshot in the storage system.
Dynamic: the volume handle of the source volume (for dynamically-created content).
Bidirectional binding reference to the VolumeSnapshot that owns this content.

VolumeSnapshotClass.description: Defines the driver and parameters for taking VolumeSnapshots — the snapshot equivalent of StorageClass. Cluster-scoped. Multiple classes can exist for different snapshot tiers (e.g. fast vs. archive).

keyFields.description: CSI driver that handles snapshot operations. Must match the CSI driver managing your PVs (e.g. ebs.csi.aws.com).
Delete: snapshot removed from storage when VolumeSnapshotContent is deleted. Retain: snapshot preserved in storage (must be cleaned up manually).
Driver-specific options for snapshot creation (e.g. type=io1, location=us-east-1). Passed directly to the CSI driver.
Set to 'true' to make this the default VolumeSnapshotClass used when no class is specified in a VolumeSnapshot.
